category_title: Children who resist teacher instructions and break classroom rules
minimal_context: The student is expected to participate in a group building activity with peers in the classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for our group activity. Please sit with your classmates and build together with the toys.

STUDENT: (Frowns, getting angry easily) No, I don't want to.

TUTOR: You need to follow instructions and join the group activity now.

STUDENT: (Starts running aimlessly around the classroom, disturbing the group activity) No!

TUTOR: Please come back here and play nicely with the others.

STUDENT: (Loses temper, runs over to the group, snatches a toy from another child, breaks it, and pushes the child) I said no!

options.A: Provide a clear beginning and end for each group building activity to structure the student's participation and transitions within the classroom setting.
options.B: Provide simultaneous stimulation of nonverbal communication from the perspective of total communication to support the student during classroom group building activities.
options.C: Enroll the student in specialized training programs, such as the Triple E Program, BEST in CLASS, and the Behavior Expectation Discrepancy Tool (B-EDT).
options.D: Implement a healing-lake visualization, whereby the student is encouraged to carefully observe the lake and notice that it is always changing, yet always itself.
